initiatives.title: DnD phone tests
initiatives.description: The DnD rebuild's phone acceptance pass: every drag surface checked by hand on a real phone against the deployed app. Split out of the desktop manual review of #3664 at the user's direction, so phone testing is the last thing the series does and is started by hand.

initiatives.title: Headless Orchestrator + Engine View
initiatives.description: Make orchestration need no babysitting and be visible. The engine drives a Claude session it owns instead of the Primary waiting on it (no waiter, no relaunch, no time limit); the engine publishes its runtime state so the Darwin UI can show every machine's engine; and lead/subscriber handoff is hardened after the first dual-machine run on 2026-10-21. Grew out of the 2026-10-20 measurement that no interactive-session primitive both streams events and lives indefinitely.

initiatives.title: Orchestration Engine 2: clean core + visualizer
initiatives.description: A clean, rule-driven orchestration engine whose every decision is visible in Darwin, replacing an engine the user could only watch through scattered terminal dashboards. The engine becomes a pure decide() function proven by a scenario corpus that runs with no database and no UI, publishes one decision record and one health heartbeat per cycle, is switched on and off from the UI, and hands launches to an executor so nobody babysits it. The visualizer is the UI: an engine view for decisions, health, locations and limits; a condensed lock view of every plan, initiative and epic; and an overlay on the plan view showing predicted order and limits. Supersedes the 'Headless Orchestrator + Engine View' initiative, which stays paused as the record of the earlier path. Hazard: the old engine must keep orchestrating until the retire epic, so nothing here edits pipeline2_engine.py in place.

epics.title: Foundation + Plan view
epics.notes: Lays the shared engine and press timeline and proves the feel on the most-used surface. The user approves the feel here before it is copied anywhere else.

epics.title: Swarm cards, Recurrin
epics.notes: Copies the shipped foundation onto the remaining react-dnd surfaces and removes react-dnd. Builds on the foundation's code, and the Recurring page shares the Plan view's tab-switch store.

epics.title: Editors, ViewBar, Test Plans, calendar
epics.notes: Moves the pangea surfaces and removes that library. Uses the shared drop policy and E2E helper as they stand after the react-dnd removal; auto-scroll and keyboard drag must not regress.

epics.title: Plan canvas
epics.notes: Gives the Konva canvas touch and the shared press timeline. Konva shapes are not DOM nodes, so the canvas keeps its own hit-testing; the box-to-epic seat drag routes the shared engine through that hit-test.

epics.title: Headless experiment
epics.notes: Measures whether a stream-json Claude session can be the orchestration receiver before anything is built on it. Kept as its own epic on 2026-10-21 so the engine-view chain never waits on the experiment (user decision).

epics.title: Engine state snapshot
epics.notes: Gives the database, and so the Darwin UI, a view of each engine's runtime state by riding the heartbeat every engine already writes. Everything that shows or reacts to engine state builds on the shape this epic defines.

epics.title: Lead/subscriber handoff hardening
epics.notes: Hardens the handoff between machines after its first real use on 2026-10-21. It edits the same engine and reservation code the snapshot work edits, which is why the two cannot run at the same time.

epics.title: Engine view in Darwin
epics.notes: The operator's view of every machine's engine once orchestration no longer lives in a terminal. It renders the snapshot's shape, and it shares the plan view's orchestration-holder code with the handoff work's browser copy of the role rules, so it follows that work rather than racing it.

epics.title: Headless orchestrator build
epics.notes: Replaces the per-wake waiter with a Claude session the engine drives, built to what the experiment measured. It cannot start before the experiment's verdict, and it edits the same engine code as the handoff work.

epics.title: Charter: rules, interfaces, coverage map
epics.notes: Everything downstream builds to the rules and the coverage map written here, which is why it is the checkpoint: the user approves the rules before any code.

epics.title: Scenario model
epics.notes: The engine's decision logic exists first as a pure function with a corpus, so the live process is a shell around something already proven; it edits none of the live engine.

epics.title: Data contract
epics.notes: The one shape every consumer reads: visualizer, supervisor, executor. Fixed before any of them so three builders do not invent three records.

epics.title: Engine process
epics.notes: Rebuilt on the model and the contract rather than patched: the old engine stays runnable until the retire epic so orchestration never goes dark mid-initiative.

epics.title: Lifecycle: on/off + supervisor
epics.notes: The UI cannot start a process, so on/off needs a reconciler on each machine; it needs only the contract, not the new engine, so it can proceed alongside the core build.

epics.title: Executor
epics.notes: Closes the babysitting gap the engine's decide-only rule leaves open; it needs real decision records to consume, so it follows the engine process.

epics.title: Engine view
epics.notes: Renders the decision record as a user reads it; it needs live records to be meaningful, so it follows the engine process.

epics.title: Lock view
epics.notes: Needs only locks, claims and the holder shape from the contract, so it can run early alongside the engine work.

epics.title: Plan view engine overlay
epics.notes: Needs the on/off mechanism and real decision records for the predicted order; the engine-off prediction uses the server-side launch queue so it works without an engine.

epics.title: Retire old engine + dashboards
epics.notes: Removes what the views and the contract replace; each removal cites the test that proved the replacement, and the docs stop describing the old mechanism.

epics.title: Coverage audit
epics.notes: The audit that every row in the charter's map is green; the one gate on calling the initiative done.
